parameters.content:
## Run the lifecycle

Click **Execute workflow**. It starts from **Change opened** and runs four pinned changes through one intake policy. The ones that ship go through the release gate. Read each node's output by title.

1. README typo ships, the release is healthy, and the loop closes.
2. Footer typo ships, production is a little worse, and the loop watches it.
3. Payments migration is held for design, the design is signed off, the error rate spikes, and the loop reopens it as a checkout outage. On-call is paged. The recovery signal closes it.
4. The unsure CSV bug stops at a person.

**Walk the lifecycle** carries the same four pins. **Deploy alert** is pinned with a checkout-down signal, and **Error-budget poll** fires a healthy probe. Pick either from the trigger menu. Both finish in the editor.

The stand-in picks answers from phrases in the state. The rules pick the action.

## Three rulesets, one vocabulary

**Intake policy.** Page a confident incident whose blast radius is at least `wide_blast` (2). Hold when design is at least `medium_confidence` (0.7) or the blast radius is that wide. Ship a confident narrow bugfix or feature. Anything else goes to a person.

**Design gate.** Approval at least `high_confidence` (0.85), residual risk below `wide_blast`, and ready to implement at least `medium_confidence` → an implementer. Otherwise a person.

**Release gate.** Roll back and reopen when the signal is degraded or an outage, the release caused it, rollback is safe, and customer impact is at least `wide_blast`. Page a confident outage that did not take that path. Close a healthy signal. Watch a narrow degradation.

The same threshold names are on every node. A Thresholds row on one node moves that number for that stage only.

## What arms production

**Change opened** is `POST /webhook/sdlc-intake`. Body fields: `title`, `state`, `design_state`, `monitor_state`, `reopen_state`, `reopen_monitor`. The editor pin is the four changes, so Execute runs them instead of waiting for a test call.

**Deploy alert** is `POST /webhook/sdlc-monitor`. Body field `state` is the signal. The editor pin is a checkout-down alert, which pages. A live spike with `reopen_state` rolls back into the intake policy.

**Error-budget poll** is a schedule, every hour. In the editor it sends a healthy probe through the release gate immediately.

The workflow is inactive, so the schedule and both webhooks are not armed. Activate it when you want those triggers live. A live POST uses the request body. From this machine the base is http://localhost:5678.

## The release comes back as a change

**Reopen the change** connects back to **Change context**. The new state is the production failure. The next monitor text is the recovery check. `pass` goes from 0 to 1.

The first pass of the payments migration rolls back. The second pass is the checkout outage: page, then the recovery signal closes. A second rollback would stop on **Loop stopped** instead of opening another pass.

An incident that starts as an outage takes **Page on-call** and still reaches the release gate, so a page is not the end of the loop.

work_type.instructions: What kind of work is this

criteria.incident: Customers are blocked or a service is down
criteria.bugfix: Correct broken behavior, small and specific
criteria.feature: New behavior or a structural change
criteria.unclear: The request does not say what to do

blast_radius.instructions: How wide is the blast radius if we act on this
criteria: One file or a copy change
Payments, security, or hard to reverse

needs_design.instructions: A design review should happen before anyone implements this

needs_human.instructions: A person should look at this before any automated action

default_action.reason: Not confident enough to act on {{answers.work_type.choice}} ({{answers.work_type.confidence}})

rules.description: A confident incident with a wide blast radius pages on-call
A wide blast radius or a design signal is held before implementation

action.reason: Hold for design. Blast radius {{answers.blast_radius.score}}, needs_design {{answers.needs_design.noul}}

rules.description: A confident, narrow bugfix or feature can go to an implementer

design_approved.instructions: The design is approved to implement

residual_risk.instructions: Residual risk if this design is implemented
criteria: Payments, security, or hard to reverse

ready_to_implement.instructions: An implementer can start from this design

default_action.reason: Design is not ready to build (approval {{answers.design_approved.noul}})

rules.description: An approved design with limited residual risk can be implemented
